reason: The text explicitly establishes and emphasizes a hierarchical structure at multiple levels: (1) Divine authority - God commands Moses as His chosen representative; (2) Leadership hierarchy - Moses is appointed to lead the Israelites with Aaron as his subordinate spokesman ('Aaron will be your mouth and you will be to him as God' - וְהָיָה הוּא יִֽהְיֶה־ לְּךָ לְפֶה וְאַתָּה תִּֽהְיֶה־ לּוֹ לֵֽאלֹהִֽים); (3) Institutional structure - Moses and Aaron are to gather and communicate with the elders of Israel, establishing a chain of authority from God through the appointed leaders to the people; (4) Obedience framework - emphasis on the people listening to and believing the appointed leaders (וַֽיַּאֲמֵ֖ן הָעָ֑ם וַֽיִּשְׁמְע֡וּ - 'the people believed and listened'). The text validates and encourages this hierarchical order as necessary and divinely ordained.
story: Moses meets Yahweh in the Burning Bush
